name: South Korea
governanceModel: First comprehensive cross-sector AI law, paired with a state-backed sovereign model push
debateTopics: AI Basic Act enforcement decree's narrow high-risk definition
Sovereign foundation-model push vs. matching frontier performance
overview:
South Korea's AI Basic Act took effect on 22 January 2026 — described by multiple legal commentators as the world's first comprehensive, cross-sector AI legal framework — with the Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) enforcing a roughly one-year grace period on fines and investigations (with exceptions for serious harm) while substantive compliance duties apply immediately.

Alongside binding regulation, MSIT launched a sovereign foundation-model programme offering state-subsidised compute, originally selecting five teams — Naver Cloud, Upstage, SK Telecom, NC AI and LG AI Research — with an early reported target of matching at least 95% of frontier-model performance, reassessed roughly every six months through 2027. That roster has since shifted: following a first-round evaluation announced 15 January 2026, MSIT dropped Naver Cloud (reportedly found to be fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen model rather than developing independently) and NC AI, leaving LG AI Research, SK Telecom and Upstage to advance; a Motif Technologies-led consortium was added via a supplementary call on 20 February 2026 to fill a vacated slot, making the programme's current roster four teams. A second-round evaluation was reportedly planned for early August 2026 to decide which teams advance further. Separately, civil society groups and human-rights lawyers have criticised the Act's enforcement decree for defining 'high-risk AI' too narrowly, arguing it offers weak protection against AI impersonation and fraud.

currentDirection.summary: South Korea moved among the fastest of major economies to pass comprehensive, binding, cross-sector AI legislation — though civil-society critics argue the enforcement decree's narrow 'high-risk' definition undercuts the law's practical bite — even as the state pours resources into a sovereign foundation-model push whose roster has already been reshuffled once, with two of the original five teams dropped and a new one added within weeks of the law taking effect.

recentDevelopments.text: The sovereign foundation-model programme's second-round evaluation is scheduled for 8-11 August 2026, with the four remaining teams (LG AI Research, SK Telecom, Upstage and Motif Technologies) tested — reportedly including a panel of around 200 'citizen evaluators' — with agentic capability and real-world applicability cited as key criteria; the round is expected to narrow the field from four teams to three, and to two finalists by year-end.

South Korea's state-backed AI compute build-out accelerates: a national AI computing centre at Solasido in Haenam, Jeollanam-do — planned around 15,000 GPUs under a public-private special-purpose company — breaks ground in the third quarter of 2026, and MSIT's 2026 AI budget rises to a reported record of roughly $3.5B, with national GPU-procurement targets of 52,000 by 2028 and 260,000 by 2030.

A 40+ expert Task Force (convened since March, reportedly still active) continues refining AI Basic Act implementation; a new ₩763.2B Science and Technology Innovation Fund and an ₩8.6 trillion R&D plan are reported, though these figures come from a general ministry source rather than a specific release.

MSIT selects a Motif Technologies-led consortium to fill the sovereign foundation-model programme's vacated fourth slot via a supplementary call, after Naver Cloud and NC AI declined to re-enter a revival round; the programme's teams are now LG AI Research, SK Telecom, Upstage and Motif Technologies.

MSIT drops Naver Cloud and NC AI from the sovereign foundation-model programme after a first-round evaluation — Naver Cloud's submission reportedly relied on fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen model rather than independent development — while LG AI Research, SK Telecom and Upstage advance to the second round.

MSIT originally selects five teams — Naver Cloud, Upstage, SK Telecom, NC AI and LG AI Research — to build homegrown sovereign foundation models with state-subsidised compute, with an early reported target of matching at least 95% of frontier-model performance, reassessed roughly every six months through 2027 (this roster and cadence were later superseded — see subsequent entries).

Civil society groups and human-rights lawyers criticise the AI Basic Act's enforcement decree for a narrow 'high-risk AI' definition, arguing it offers weak protection against AI impersonation and fraud.

policyAndRegulation.title: AI Basic Act
policyAndRegulation.summary: Act on the Development of AI and Establishment of Trust — described by multiple legal commentators as the world's first comprehensive cross-sector AI legal framework, in force since 22 January 2026 with a roughly one-year grace period on fines and investigations (exceptions apply for serious harm).

researchEcosystem.summary: South Korea's sovereign-model push runs through a state-backed foundation-model programme — currently LG AI Research, SK Telecom, Upstage and Motif Technologies — building homegrown models with subsidised compute. Two of the programme's original five teams, Naver Cloud and NC AI, were dropped after a January 2026 evaluation and replaced by a Motif Technologies-led consortium in February 2026. Earlier reporting cited a target of matching at least 95% of frontier-model performance, reassessed roughly every six months, though this has not been independently reconfirmed since the reshuffle.

debates.topic: AI Basic Act enforcement decree's narrow high-risk definition
debates.summary: Some civil-society groups and human-rights lawyers argue the Act's implementing decree defines 'high-risk AI' too narrowly, leaving what they characterise as weak protection against AI impersonation and fraud.
debates.expanded: Human-rights lawyers and civil-society groups say the enforcement decree's scope — relying mainly on watermarking requirements and fines — is too limited given the scale of AI-enabled fraud and impersonation risks. Some industry voices counter that a stricter definition would undercut Korea's competitiveness just as it is trying to build sovereign frontier capability. The precise wording and full scope of the decree's 'high-risk AI' definition were not independently verified against the Korean-language legal text for this summary; the characterisation above relies on secondary legal-commentary and NGO sources.

debates.topic: Sovereign foundation-model push vs. matching frontier performance
debates.summary: Korea's state-backed sovereign-model programme — now four teams after two were dropped and one added in early 2026 — has been reported (though not fully reconfirmed since the reshuffle) to be held to a target of matching a high share of frontier-model performance on a periodic review cycle.
debates.expanded: Unlike open-ended national AI investment elsewhere, Korea's programme was reported to carry a specific, numeric performance target — at least 95% of frontier-model performance — reassessed roughly every six months through 2027, creating pressure on participants to show measurable progress against US and Chinese frontier labs rather than simply receiving indefinite state support. That pressure appears to have already had consequences: after a first-round evaluation announced 15 January 2026, MSIT dropped Naver Cloud and NC AI (Naver Cloud's submission reportedly relied on fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen model rather than independent development), leaving LG AI Research, SK Telecom and Upstage to advance. A Motif Technologies-led consortium was added on 20 February 2026 to fill the vacated slot, and the second-round evaluation is scheduled for 8-11 August 2026 — reportedly weighting agentic capability and real-world applicability, and using a panel of around 200 'citizen evaluators' — expected to narrow the four teams to three, with two finalists chosen by year-end. That contest is unfolding alongside a rapid state-backed compute build-out (a national AI computing centre at Haenam and a record 2026 AI budget), underscoring how contested, and unsettled, the sovereign-model bet remains.
